jurisdiction.name: Brunei Darussalam
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Brunei governs AI mainly through soft law: the Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry's (AITI) voluntary Guide on AI Governance and Ethics (2025, second edition 2026 covering generative AI) and the Data and AI Strategy in the Digital Brunei 2030 plan (2026), with education ministry guidance on generative AI. Binding sector rules adopted in 2026 add AI duties: Cyber Security Brunei's code of practice and AI security guidelines for critical information infrastructure, and the central bank's (BDCB) fair-treatment notice covering AI in credit assessment, effective 2027. The Personal Data Protection Order 2025 has been in force since January 2026 but has no AI-specific provisions.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. A national AI strategy listed in the trade ministry's 2026-2030 plan has not been published and is listed as a lead.

instruments.summary: Public consultation draft, issued by AITI on 9 July 2024 with a Public Consultation Paper, of a national guide for organisations that design, develop, deploy and/or use AI in Brunei Darussalam. It describes the AI system lifecycle, sets guiding principles (transparency and explainability, data protection and data governance, security and safety, robustness, fairness and equity, human centricity, accountability and integrity) and proposes an AI governance framework built on people, process (internal governance and risk management) and technology (testing, validation).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Consultation stage of Brunei's national AI governance and ethics guide.
instruments.current_status: Consultation closed; AITI reports feedback from 17 respondents. Replaced by the final Guide issued 11 April 2025 (now itself followed by a Second Edition, 2026). Kept for the timeline.

instruments.publisher_name: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry of Brunei Darussalam
instruments.summary: Brunei's first national, voluntary guide on AI governance and ethics, developed by AITI with a 25-member working group after the July 2024 consultation. It is technology- and sector-agnostic and gives organisations that design, develop, deploy and/or use AI seven guiding principles (transparency and explainability, data protection and data governance, security and safety, robustness and reliability, fairness and equity, human centricity, accountability and integrity) plus an AI governance framework covering people, process and technology. AITI states the principles align with the ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Brunei's national baseline AI governance and ethics guidance.
instruments.current_status: Released 11 April 2025 (AITI press release, issued in Malay and English). AITI's AI Governance and Ethics page now also lists a Second Edition (2026), which is treated as replacing this first edition.

instruments.official_title: Guide on Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Ethics for Brunei Darussalam, Second Edition
instruments.english_title: Guide on Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Ethics for Brunei Darussalam (Second Edition)
instruments.issuing_authority: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry of Brunei Darussalam, with the AI Governance and Ethics Working Group
instruments.publisher_name: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry of Brunei Darussalam
instruments.summary: Updated edition of Brunei's national voluntary AI governance and ethics guide, adding a chapter on advances in AI and its risks, generative-AI definitions and risk-mitigation measures for generative AI (e.g. content verification), and links to the Personal Data Protection Order, 2025. It keeps the seven guiding principles and the people-process-technology governance framework (risk assessments, human involvement scaled to risk, testing and validation, reference to ISO/IEC 42001 and the NIST AI RMF) and adds Brunei use cases, including the Ministry of Education's generative AI guidance. The working group now lists 31 member organisations, including MTIC, MOH, MOFE, MOE, MINDEF, EGNC, Cyber Security Brunei and BDCB.

instruments.publisher_name: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry of Brunei Darussalam
instruments.summary: Brunei's first general data protection law, governing the collection, use and disclosure of personal data by organisations (private sector), with consent, purpose-limitation, access and correction, protection, breach-notification and accountability obligations. AITI is the administering and enforcing Authority. It has no AI-specific or automated-decision provisions, but it governs personal data used to train and operate AI systems, and AITI's Second Edition AI Guide requires compliance with it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding data protection baseline for AI systems processing personal data.
instruments.current_status: Gazetted 8 January 2025 (S 1/2025); under s.1 it commences on dates appointed by ministerial notification. The Sultan's titah (2025) states it was consented to come into force on 1 January 2026.

instruments.official_title: Digital Brunei 2030: The Digital Brunei Transformation Plan
instruments.english_title: Digital Brunei 2030: The Digital Brunei Transformation Plan (incl. the Data and Artificial Intelligence Strategy)
instruments.summary: Five-year national digital masterplan (2026-2030), formulated with the Sultan's consent and succeeding the Digital Economy Masterplan 2025; it combines a Digital Government, Digital Society and Digital Business Strategy with a cross-cutting Data and Artificial Intelligence Strategy. The Data & AI Strategy aims to 'build comprehensive foundations for a robust AI ecosystem', with principles such as 'adopt intentionally, temper the hype' and preserving Melayu Islam Beraja, and initiatives on policy, safety and security (continued review of the AI Governance and Ethics guidelines, adoption of AI testing frameworks, secure-by-design, a sovereign cloud policy, a data and AI maturity framework), an AI-capable data centre, sovereign cloud with AI compute, a Brunei-context national large language model, civil-service upskilling and generative-AI pilots in government. Key success measures include public- and private-sector AI pilot projects and improved public-sector data and AI maturity.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national strategy containing Brunei's Data and AI Strategy.
instruments.current_status: Released by the Digital Brunei Council on 2 June 2026 (MTIC announcement); implementation is overseen by the Council.

instruments.official_title: Generative AI (GenAI) Guidance for Education: Handbook Edition
instruments.english_title: Generative AI (GenAI) Guidance for Education: Handbook Edition
instruments.summary: Ministry of Education guidance on the responsible and ethical use of generative AI by school and higher-education leaders, administrators, educators, learners, parents and guardians. It sets seven principles for ethical AI in education grounded in Melayu Islam Beraja and Maqasid Syariah (purpose, compliance, knowledge, balance, integrity, agency, evaluation), an AI readiness pathway and expectations such as disclosing AI use in student work. It aligns with the MOE Digital Transformation Plan 2023-2027, AITI's Guide on AI Governance and Ethics and the UNESCO AI competency frameworks.

instruments.official_title: Notice on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers (Notice No. CE/N-1/2026/1)
instruments.english_title: Notice to Banks and Financial Institutions on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers (CE/N-1/2026/1)
instruments.summary: Binding conduct notice issued under section 54 of the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank Order, 2010 to all banks and financial institutions, requiring fair treatment of financial consumers and the integration of conduct risk into risk management. Among the measures for vulnerable consumers, para 4.16(d) requires institutions to exercise caution when using artificial intelligence in credit assessments or risk underwriting to avoid unfair discrimination, excessive pricing or exclusion of vulnerable consumers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only identified binding financial-sector provision on AI use in Brunei.
instruments.current_status: Issued 31 August 2026; takes effect 1 March 2027. General conduct notice with a single explicit AI clause.

instruments.official_title: Cybersecurity Code of Practice for Critical Information Infrastructure (Version 2.0)
instruments.english_title: Cybersecurity Code of Practice for Critical Information Infrastructure, Version 2.0 (AI clause 3.8)
instruments.summary: Code of practice under the Cybersecurity Act with which owners of designated Critical Information Infrastructure must comply (s.13 of the Act). Version 2.0 adds clause 3.8 on the use of AI systems and services: CII owners remain accountable for AI used within or against the CII, must adopt an AI security policy (acceptable uses, permitted tools, human-in-the-loop or oversight, data governance), assess AI systems before deployment or major change, apply specific controls to generative, agentic and autonomous AI, and bring AI systems under logging, monitoring and incident response.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding AI security requirements for critical information infrastructure.
instruments.current_status: Version 2.0 dated 15 September 2026 (CSB news item dated 14 September 2026); the Code was first issued as Version 1.0 on 11 March 2024 without AI provisions. The compliance date for the new clauses was not identified.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): PDF (HTTP 200) read with pdftotext; revision history 'Version 2.0, 15/09/2026, inclusion of AI security policy (generative/agentic/autonomous AI) and a Secure by Design clause'; s.1.4 legal effect (s.13 of the Act); CSB news item of 14 Sep 2026 read.

instruments.english_title: AI Security Policy Guidelines (Cyber Security Brunei)
instruments.summary: Policy guideline complementing the CII Code of Practice that sets baseline controls for secure adoption of AI, with dedicated controls for generative, agentic and autonomous AI. It covers AI security policy, acceptable use, human-in-the-loop oversight, data and model governance, model and supply-chain security, logging and incident response, training, procurement and contractual requirements, standards alignment and annual compliance review, plus lifecycle control gates. It states compliance is mandatory for CII owners for AI used within or against the CII and serves as a recommended national guideline for other organisations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National AI security guidance from the cyber authority, including AI procurement requirements.
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0, first release 15 September 2026. Stated to be mandatory for designated CII owners and a recommended national baseline for non-CII organisations.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): PDF (HTTP 200, 41 pages) read with pdftotext; document history 'Version 1.0, 15 September 2026, First Release'; linked from CSB's Additional References page and news item of 14 Sep 2026.

instruments.official_title: Guide on Responsible Use of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI), Series 1: Goal-Oriented Prompting
instruments.english_title: Guide on Responsible Use of Agentic AI, Series 1: Goal-Oriented Prompting (First Edition, September 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry of Brunei Darussalam, with the AI Governance and Ethics Working Group
instruments.publisher_name: Authority for Info-communications Technology Industry of Brunei Darussalam
instruments.summary: Public guide from AITI, developed with the AI Governance and Ethics Working Group, on using agentic AI tools responsibly, focused on goal-oriented prompting. It explains how to write prompts that set a persona, objectives, permissions and tools, parameters and an execution flow, urges least-privilege access for AI agents, and calls for human-in-the-loop checkpoints before higher-risk steps, in particular religious advice, cultural and social context (the Malay Islamic Monarchy philosophy), legal procedures, financial transactions and medical advice. It closes with ethical-prompting cautions and a do's-and-don'ts list for before, during and after prompting.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National guidance on safe use of agentic AI by the public, part of AITI's AI governance and ethics series.
instruments.current_status: First edition, dated September 2026 on its cover, listed on AITI's Guidebooks page with a Malay version (Panduan Penggunaan Agentic AI Secara Bertanggungjawab Siri 1). The guide says it may be amended periodically; it is not legal advice and is not binding.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National law, the government, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying documents were found for transparency, standards, regulatory sandboxes, indices and readiness or international instruments. Some official documents were unavailable or no longer online, so the data protection order's commencement notice and the release date of the AI guide's second edition remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. agc.gov.bn gazette copy of S 1/2025 and the PDPO commencement notification 404 (commencement from the Sultan's titah quoted on the Digital Brunei Council site); AITI PDP guidance listing loads dynamically; Digital Economy Masterplan 2025 PDF 404. Digital Brunei 2030 booklet text not extractable (content checked on the official Data & AI Strategy page). Second Edition of the AI Guide dated by year only. Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Personal Data Protection Order, 2025 read (no AI or automated-decision provisions; recorded as the data protection baseline). AGC site reached but its gazette PDF path for S 1/2025 returned 404; a site search of agc.gov.bn for 'artificial intelligence' found nothing. No AI law or AI bill found. Cybersecurity Act (Chapter 272) is not AI-specific (its CII Code of Practice v2.0 with AI clause recorded).; Government: Digital Brunei Council / Digital Brunei 2030 incl. Data & AI Strategy recorded (released 2 June 2026). Digital Economy Masterplan 2025 (2020): official MTIC PDF now 404 and the MTIC library item now points to Digital Brunei 2030, so it was not recorded (historical, AI content not verified). MTIC Strategic Plan 2026-2030 read: ministry corporate plan with only passing AI mentions (lists a National AI Strategy as an initiative, held as a lead). No national public-sector/civil-service AI guideline found (EGNC site checked; nothing AI-specific). No government AI readiness index, standards adoption, algorithm register or AI sandbox found.; Ministries: Education: GenAI Guidance for Education (2025) recorded. AITI 2nd-edition guide lists MOH, MOFE, MINDEF, MOD, MCYS as working-group members, but no AI documents of their own were found in searches. Universities' internal GenAI policies (UBD, UTB) excluded as institutional policies.; Regulators: AITI (AI guide draft/1st/2nd editions; PDP Order). BDCB: Notice on Fair Treatment of Financial Consumers with AI clause recorded; FinTech Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines (2017/2020) not AI-specific; AI fake-news public alerts excluded. Cyber Security Brunei: CII Code of Practice v2.0 and AI Security Policy Guidelines recorded. AITI PDP guidance-documents page loads dynamically and showed no AI-specific guidance.. Not reached: agc.gov.bn Government Gazette copy of S 1/2025 and PDPO commencement notification (404); AITI PDP 'Guidance Documents' listing (dynamic page; no items rendered); Digital Economy Masterplan 2025 official PDF (mtic.gov.bn path 404). Could not verify: PDPO commencement notification (gazette); Digital Brunei 2030 booklet text (image-based PDF); strategy content verified from the official web pages; Exact release date of AITI Guide Second Edition; Digital Economy Masterplan 2025 AI content (official PDF no longer online). transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, international: no material found.
